description: Provider-neutral canonical performance specification for one TTS synthesis chunk. Produced by the Performance Director from semantic analysis of the script. NEVER store provider-specific tags (e.g. Alibaba emotion markup) here; compile semantic performance to provider controls in the Provider Compiler step. Every generated chunk MUST have an explicit performance state: there is no default-inherited emotion, so omit nothing the director decided.

examples.text: Here is the part nobody talks about. The local model was never the product. It was the practice field.

transition_from_previous.note: story beat ends, claim lands with gravity

transition_to_next.note: after the claim, opens into the how question

chunk_id.description: Stable identifier for this chunk, e.g. 'ep042-c007'. Used by the QC gate, intent ledger, and regeneration policy to refer to exactly one chunk.

confidence.description: Delivery certainty: how sure the speaker sounds about what is said. 0.0 = hesitant/hedging, 1.0 = absolute declarative certainty. The NOLAN_CONFIDENT_HUMAN_V1 baseline is high (0.7-0.9) except where the text itself is genuinely tentative.

emotion.description: Canonical semantic emotion for this chunk, provider-neutral. The compiler maps this to provider controls (e.g. persistent emotion tags). This is the single most important expressive field: pick the emotion the MEANING calls for, never decoration.

emotion_intensity.description: How strongly the emotion is performed, 0.0 (barely colored) to 1.0 (peak moment). Bands: 0.0-0.2 subtle background coloring; 0.2-0.5 natural noticeable modulation; 0.5-0.75 strong, intentional moment; 0.75-1.0 peak, reserved for the episode's genuine high points. Distribution target across an episode: 65-75% of chunks at/below 0.3, 20-30% in 0.3-0.6, 5-10% above 0.6 (starting heuristics, see emotion_mapping.md).

emphasis.description: Words or short phrases to emphasize, in order of appearance. Emphasis without shouting: weight 1 = light stress, 2 = clear emphasis, 3 = the single most important word in the chunk (use at most one weight-3 per chunk). Empty array = let natural prosody carry it.

span.description: Exact substring of text to emphasize. Must appear verbatim in text.

weight.description: Emphasis strength: 1 light, 2 clear, 3 the single peak word of the chunk.

energy.description: Vocal energy independent of emotion: 0.0 = low, near-quiet intensity; 0.5 = relaxed conversational baseline; 1.0 = full broadcast energy. Controlled energy is a profile trait: most narration lives 0.35-0.6. Values above 0.8 need scene justification (PAYOFF, genuine excitement).

episode_id.description: Episode or script identifier this chunk belongs to. Optional but recommended for continuity across chunks.

order_index.description: Zero-based position of this chunk in the episode. The compiler and QC use this to locate the previous/next chunk for transition and boundary checks.

pace.description: Relative speaking rate multiplier, 1.0 = the voice's natural baseline. 0.80-1.25 is the absolute envelope; ordinary narration stays 0.92-1.08. Anything outside 0.9-1.1 must be justified by scene_type (e.g. WARNING slows, SURPRISING_RESULT quickens slightly). Microprosody law: pace is a deliberate choice per chunk, never random wobble.

pause_density.description: How much intra-chunk pausing the director wants: 0.0 = nearly no added pauses (dense technical run), 0.5 = natural thought-boundary pauses, 1.0 = heavily punctuated, deliberate cadence (serious claims, reveals). Pauses follow punctuation and semantic structure (new thought, important claim, rhetorical question, contrast, reveal, topic transition). NEVER mechanical identical silence after every sentence.

pitch_bias.description: Relative pitch offset in approximate semitones from the voice baseline. Positive = slightly higher, negative = slightly lower. Ordinary speech stays within [-1.0, 1.0]. Values beyond +/-1.0 require explicit director justification and listener review (the deeper-voice dimension is benchmarked, never pushed until synthetic).

pronunciation_overrides.description: Terms in text whose pronunciation needs a provider-layer fix. The canonical source of truth is pronunciation_lexicon.md; this field only overrides or adds per-chunk entries. Never rewrite the script text to trick the TTS.

pronunciation.description: Plain-English pronunciation guidance, e.g. 'eff why dee'. The provider compiler turns this into hot_fix entries.

term.description: Term exactly as it appears in text.

scene_type.description: The semantic function this chunk plays in the episode. Drives the default emotion via emotion_mapping.md and shapes pacing and pausing. Keep the taxonomy small; use OTHER only when nothing fits and add a note.

seed_policy.description: Reproducibility policy for this chunk. REGRESSION MODE: fixed seed so changes can be compared fairly. PERFORMANCE MODE: ordinary narration uses a stable seed; hero lines get 2-3 candidates from the approved bank, scored, winner cached. NEVER randomize every chunk independently (personality drift).

bank_id.description: Approved seed-bank identifier for performance_bank mode.

candidate_count.description: Number of candidates to generate for hero_candidates mode. 2-3 per the directive.

text.description: The exact prose to synthesize for this chunk. Plain script text only: NO provider markup, NO pronunciation trickery (use pronunciation_overrides), NO SSML. Prefer semantic chunks (paragraph, complete thought, mini-scene); do NOT split at every sentence.

transition_from_previous.description: How this chunk connects to the previous chunk's emotional state. strategy: 'continue' (same state), 'soften' (lower intensity of same/similar emotion), 'shift' (different emotion, smooth bridge), 'reset' (deliberate clean break at a topic boundary). previous_emotion is required when order_index > 0.

note.description: Short director note on why this transition is right, e.g. 'topic change, drop the amusement cleanly'.

previous_emotion.description: The emotion of the previous chunk, so the compiler can shape the bridge.

transition_to_next.description: What the director anticipates after this chunk. Lets the compiler shape trailing cadence (e.g. a rising inflection before a reveal, a settled ending before reflection). Same strategy vocabulary as transition_from_previous.

next_emotion.description: The anticipated emotion of the next chunk.

note.description: Short director note, e.g. 'ends on a question, next chunk answers it'.

vocal_event.description: A one-shot vocal event the director explicitly authored into this chunk. These are RARE: a vocal_event must have a clear semantic justification (genuine laughter beat, real sigh at a setback). Null = none. Provider compilers render these as one-shot vocal tags; they must never appear randomly.

title: PerformanceSpec
